title: Big Brains and Changing Environments: Cause or Consequence?
abstract: arXiv:2609.15569v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large brains are metabolically costly, and associations with changing environments do not imply they evolved there, as the Cognitive Buffer Hypothesis (CBH) would suggest. They may instead evolve in stable conditions and later facilitate colonization of changing environments. Using neuro-evolution in an artificial seasonal foraging task, we compared agents evolving exclusively in changing environments to agents first evolved in static environments before transitioning. Results show that larger neural networks in dynamic environments arise mainly from prior static evolution, achieving superior performance under unpredictable changes. Our results challenge strict CBH predictions, provide agent-based (computational) support for a colonization-based account and highlight the role of evolutionary history in brain size evolution.

translated_title: 大脑与变化环境：是原因还是结果？
translated_abstract: 大体积大脑的代谢成本高昂，而它们与变化环境之间的关联并不意味着它们是在变化环境中进化而来的，尽管认知缓冲假说（Cognitive Buffer Hypothesis, CBH）如此暗示。大体积大脑也可能是先在稳定条件下进化出来，随后才促进了生物对变化环境的扩散定居。通过在一项人工季节性觅食任务中进行神经进化实验，我们比较了完全在变化环境中进化的智能体与先在静态环境中进化、之后再过渡到变化环境的智能体。结果表明，动态环境中出现的更大规模神经网络主要源于先前的静态环境进化，并且这些网络在不可预测的环境变化下展现出更优越的性能。我们的研究结果挑战了认知缓冲假说的严格预测，为基于扩散定居的解释提供了基于智能体的（计算）证据支持，并凸显了进化历史在大脑体积演化中的重要作用。
tldr: 研究表明大体积大脑可能先在稳定环境中进化形成，随后才促进了对变化环境的扩散定居，这一结果挑战了认知缓冲假说的预测，并凸显了进化历史对脑容量演化的关键作用。
en_tdlr: Larger brains may have evolved in stable environments first and later facilitated colonization of changing environments, challenging the strict predictions of the Cognitive Buffer Hypothesis and highlighting the role of evolutionary history in brain size evolution.
